newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITIMPEKS TO CHANGE NOMINAL VALUE OF SHARES.
newsitem.headline: LITIMPEKS TO CHANGE NOMINAL VALUE OF SHARES.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank said on Thursday that it would change the nominal value of its shares leading to a decrease in its share capital.
The shares' value will be reduced from ten litas to one litas.
"The shareholders' meeting today decided to decrease the share capital of 40.9 million litas to 4.09 million litas," the bank's spokeswoman, Regina Sondeckiene, told Reuters.
She added that the bank planned to make a 56 million litas share issue to boost its share capital to 60 million litas after the split.
She also said that its 1996 losses amounted to 6.37 million litas versus 14.5 million litas the previous year.
The bank was unexpectedly shut at the end of 1995 along with another major bank, Innovation Bank, sparking a crisis in the sector.
Litimpeks managed to get back on its feet and was reopened last June while Innovation is to be liquidated.
Litimpeks said on Wednesday that Estonia's Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank were eyeing the share issue.
